title: cost-optimization: autotune batching & caching defaults; quantization profiles; unit-econ tooling
author: Ethan Morales
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost across common workloads by shipping conservative batching/caching defaults, adding model quantization profiles, and integrating basic unit-economics tooling into the optimize service. This PR implements: 1) an autotuneable defaults module that selects batching and KV-cache policies per model family and latency SLO; 2) a first set of quantization profiles (fp16, int8_fast, int8_quality) with runtime-compatible operator hints; 3) a unit-economics adapter that computes per-request cost estimates using current batching/caching/quant profiles and exposes them to the Console and Optimize UI. Includes migration and rollout plan (default off via feature flag, gradual canary to 5% then 50% then global), automated tests, and docs. Checklist: [x] implement defaults/autotune core, [x] add quant profiles and model metadata, [x] unit-econ service + API, [x] e2e tests, [x] docs and release notes, [x] canary rollout config. Performance: internal benchmark (chat-like queries, median seq=256) shows ~18% token-cost reduction and <=5% latency regression at 95th percentile on p4d for int8_fast with batching enabled. Backwards compat: all changes guarded by feature flags and model pins; no breaking API changes. Related Linear: ENG-1932, ENG-1978.

review_thread: Priya Singh (reviewer): Overall looks good; can you make the quant profile names more explicit (int8_fast -> int8_low_precision, int8_quality -> int8_high_quality) so they are discoverable in Console?

Lydia Chen (reviewer): We need an SLO safety net — if latency drifts above threshold we should auto-disable autotune for affected model-version. Suggest adding a watchdog metric and automatic disable hook.
Ethan Morales (author): Added watchdog metric runtime/autotune_latency_watchdog and automatic disable path (disabled flag surfaced in model state). Added unit test to cover disable path.
Samir Patel (security): Quick question on UEcon adapter: ensure no customer secrets are sent to Optimize service. Please confirm data flow is metadata-only.

Ethan Morales (author): Confirmed: unit-econ adapter uses only aggregated token counts, model metadata (name, seq distribution), and feature flags; no PII or customer payloads are transmitted. Added doc note and an automated test that validates no request payload includes user text.
